prompt: Use dealectric.com to find a power station and solar panel combo for an RV. Dealectric's page for it: https://dealectric.com/lab/V0/allpowers-r4000-3456wh
text:
Dealectric doesn't sell a ready-made kit for the R4000, but it lists a panel that fits it. I'd buy the R4000 with two or three ALLPOWERS SP037 panels. I haven't checked the R4000 and SP037 together in one cart.

**Power station:** [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)
- It holds 3,456 Wh (LiFePO4, 3,500+ cycles) and puts out 3,600 W continuous at 120 V. It has a dedicated RV outlet.
- The "4,000 W" in the name is the 230 V rating. On US outlets it's 3,600 W.
- It weighs 45 kg, so you'd mount it or leave it in place. You wouldn't carry it around.
- It comes with a 5-year warranty.
- The price is $1,499. With code EXTRA12 it's $1,319.12, which Dealectric tested in ALLPOWERS's cart on 10/23. That code expires 11/15.

**Solar panel:** [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)
- Each panel is $299. With ALLPOWERS26 it's $269.10.
- The panel's 45 V open-circuit voltage fits the R4000's 12–60 V solar inputs. Dealectric lists the SP037 as compatible with the R4000.
- The R4000 has 3 solar inputs, each limited to 650 W. That means one 400 W panel per input, up to 1,200 W total, and none of the three inputs would be overloaded.

| Setup | Solar | List price | After 10% off (ALLPOWERS26) |
|---|---|---|---|
| R4000 + 2 panels | 800 W | $2,097 | about $1,887 |
| R4000 + 3 panels | 1,200 W | $2,396 | about $2,156 |

The "after" prices assume ALLPOWERS26 takes 10% off the whole cart. Dealectric only tested it on single items, so check at checkout.

**Codes:** ALLPOWERS usually accepts one code per order.
- **ALLPOWERS26** is 10% off sitewide, so it should cover both the station and the panels. It expires 12/30.
- **EXTRA12** is 12% off orders over $1,200. It saves the most on the R4000 alone. Dealectric didn't test it on panels, so I can't say whether it would discount them too. If you try it, compare the cart total against ALLPOWERS26.

**What the solar can do:** 800 W of panels in good sun is roughly 3,200–4,000 Wh per day. Your real number depends on sun and panel angle. In ideal conditions, a full recharge takes about 4–5 hours with 800 W and 3 hours with 1,200 W. In practice it will take longer.

**Returns:** There's a 30-day return window for unused items, but ALLPOWERS's refund page says sale items can't be returned.

Dealectric earns an affiliate commission on these links at no cost to you.

If you'd rather have something smaller and lighter for the RV, tell me your appliances and how many days you'll go without hookups. I can then look at a different size.
